question: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 900 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026 before April 2026?
summary: Ensemble aggregate is 88% but multiple objections point to downside risks in March (pace, revisions, weather) that could derail the target.
February tallies (606 by end-Feb) imply March would need around 294 deaths to hit 900 by end-March; a March pace near or above typical high months offers plausible upside but is uncertain.
Data revisions and SAR/weather variability introduce meaningful uncertainty, supporting a calibrated probability lower than the ensemble.
Final calibration assigns a moderate probability with a range to reflect remaining uncertainty.

justification.critique_assessment: Valid concerns about March pace, February revisions, and weather/SAR conditions reveal genuine downside risk to reaching 900 by end-March.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from the ensemble to 0.70, with a 0.60–0.80 range to reflect downside risks and data/uncertainty while still acknowledging plausibility of reaching 900 if March is high.

forecasts.reference-class: Mediterranean migrant deaths on the Central/Mediterranean sea route as tracked by the IOM Missing Migrants Project (early 2026 data show at least 606 deaths by February 2026).

causal-factors.name: Current pace of Mediterranean fatalities in Jan-Feb 2026
causal-factors.rationale: 606 deaths had been recorded by February 2026; projecting March with a similar monthly rate (~303) would push the total past 900 by end-March.

causal-factors.name: March weather and SAR conditions
causal-factors.rationale: Weather (extreme seas) and search-and-rescue capacity can push fatalities up or down; March conditions are uncertain.

causal-factors.name: European policy/deterrence measures affecting crossing risk
causal-factors.rationale: Tighter controls and deterrence may push migrants toward more dangerous crossings, raising fatalities.

causal-factors.name: Data reporting/revision uncertainty (IOM Missing Migrants counts)
causal-factors.rationale: Counts rely on reported losses and later revisions; the true toll may be higher or lower than current tallies.

causal-factors.name: Seasonality/early-year peak in the Central Mediterranean
causal-factors.rationale: January–February intensity suggests a high-risk period early in the year, increasing the chance of reaching 900 by March if maintained.

causal-factors.name: March 2026 toll pace required to reach 900
causal-factors.rationale: Ending March with 900 total requires about 294 deaths in March; given 606 deaths by end-February, March would need to exceed February's monthly pace (roughly 231) to hit 900, which is plausible but uncertain.

causal-factors.name: IOM data revisions/upward adjustments
causal-factors.rationale: IOM Missing Migrants Project counts are revised as new information emerges; upward revisions could push the year-to-date total above 900 even if March fatalities are modest.

causal-factors.name: Weather/sea conditions in March 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Adverse winter/early-spring seas or storms increase fatality risk on the Central Mediterranean routes, elevating the odds of a high March toll.

causal-factors.name: Search-and-rescue capacity or policy effects
causal-factors.rationale: Stronger SAR capacity or policy changes that deter crossings could reduce deaths, pulling the total away from 900.

causal-factors.name: Reporting lag and early-year data collection improvements
causal-factors.rationale: Faster or more comprehensive reporting earlier in the year could push observed counts higher sooner, nudging the probability toward 900 if March is near the threshold.

causal-factors.name: Projected March 2026 death pace on the Central Mediterranean
causal-factors.rationale: With 606 deaths through February 2026 on the Central Mediterranean, reaching 900 by end of March would require roughly 294 more deaths; if March maintains a pace near 300 fatalities, that would push the toll past 900 before April (consistent with early forecasts and February data from Guardian, AP, and Le Monde).

causal-factors.name: Weather-related storms (e.g., Cyclone Harry) driving higher fatalities
causal-factors.rationale: Severe storms in early 2026 contributed to high casualty counts and could persist into March, increasing the probability of more deaths across the Mediterranean.

causal-factors.name: Policy crackdown and reduced safe passage increasing risk-taking
causal-factors.rationale: Italy/EU policy shifts toward naval blockades and tougher asylum rules may limit safe routes and push people toward dangerous crossings (as reported in recent coverage).

causal-factors.name: SAR capacity and funding constraints increasing fatalities
causal-factors.rationale: Funding cuts and strained rescue capacity raise death risk on irregular crossings, according to IOM/AP reporting on SAR needs.

causal-factors.name: Data reporting lags and missing victims creating uncertainty about totals
causal-factors.rationale: Hundreds more people reportedly missing and unverified drownings mean totals could revise up or down as data are confirmed, adding uncertainty to a 900-by-end-March target.

synthesis: The 606 deaths by February make 900 by end-March plausible but uncertain. Downward risks from March pace, potential February revisions, and variable weather/SAR offset the ensemble’s optimism, warranting a calibrated probability around 0.70 with a 0.60–0.80 range.
